mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS-tightening episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the median baseline at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 0.5% per month, combined with a concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals a supply-side expansion that boosts earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% and HOUST > 0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month while the federal funds rate is held constant, it signals an unmet inflation response, increasing the probability of future rate hikes and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month +0.4% AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below the baseline at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which is expected to reduce corporate revenue growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a compositional shift toward lower-quality jobs; this predicts muted earnings growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,000 units for three consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below the baseline at 90% confidence.
